```artifact
Feature: Valid Login and User Management
  As a system user
    Given a user attempts to access the system without a valid login id/username and password
    When the system checks the credentials
    Then the access should be denied with an appropriate error message

Feature: Administrator Control of User Information
  As the system administrator
    Given there are valid login credentials for a user
    When I maintain user id/login id and passwords
    Then the user information should be correctly managed and retrievable

Scenario: Virtual Clinic Main Menu
  Given the main menu is accessible
    When I navigate to the Main Menu
    Then I should see options to:
    - Maintain Speciality
    - Maintain Doctors
    - Maintain Chemist & Labs
    - Maintain Symptoms

Scenario: Administrator System Administration
  Given I am logged into the Administrator system
    When I access the Administrator System Administration screens
    Then I should be able to:
    - Set up Users/Passwords
    - Set up Control File for Pincode
    - Create Appointment File
    - View/Print Invoice
    - Perform Backups
    - Archive Patient Profiles

Scenario: Adding Speciality
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Create Users/Specialities
    When I add a new Speciality
    Then the Speciality Id, Name, and Description should be recorded correctly

Scenario: Editing and Updating Speciality
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I edit/update a Speciality
    Then the Speciality Id, Name, and Description should be displayed and modifiable

Scenario Outline: Adding and Updating Speciality Information
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I add/edit a Speciality with the following details
    And the Speciality Id, Name, and Description are entered
    Then the Speciality should be correctly added/updated in the system

  Examples:
  | Speciality Id | Speciality Name | Speciality Description       | Expected Outcome                                  |
  | example1     | exampleName1   | exampleDescription1        | Speciality should be correctly added/updated          |
  | example2     | exampleName2   | exampleDescription2        | Speciality should be correctly added/updated          |

Scenario: Accessing System with Valid Credentials
  Given I have valid login credentials
    When I access the system
    Then I should be granted access to the Virtual Clinic Main Menu

Scenario Outline: Access Denied Due to Invalid Credentials
  Given I do not have a valid login id/username and password
    When I attempt to access the system
    Then I should be denied access with an appropriate error message

  Examples:
  | No credentials | Access denied | Error message displayed    | Access should be denied                           |
  | No credentials | Yes         | Error message displayed    | Access should be denied                           |

Scenario: Non-empty Speciality Management
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I ensure that Speciality Id, Name, and Description are non-empty
    Then they should not be empty

  Examples:
  | Yes           | Yes         | Yes                   | Speciality details should not be empty             |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Adding a New Speciality
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I add a new Speciality with non-empty details
    Then the Speciality should be correctly added with non-empty details

  Examples:
  | Non-empty     | Non-empty    | Non-empty             | Speciality correctly added                        |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Editing and Updating a Speciality
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I edit/update a Speciality with non-empty details
    Then the Speciality Id, Name, and Description should be displayed and modifiable

  Examples:
  | Non-empty     | Non-empty    | Non-empty             | Speciality correctly edited/updated             |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Verifying Speciality Details
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I query a Speciality Id, Name, and Description
    Then the correct details should be displayed

  Examples:
  | Specific Id   | Specific Name | Specific Description   | Details should be correctly displayed          |
  | exampleId1   | exampleName1  | exampleDescription1    | Details should match the input             |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Ensuring Non-empty Fields
  Given I am on the Administrator Menu Screen to Maintain Specialities
    When I ensure that Speciality Id, Name, and Description are non-empty
    Then they should not be empty

  Examples:
  | Yes          | Yes         | Yes                  | Speciality details should not be empty             |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Confirming Correct Speciality Addition/Update
  Given I add/edit a Speciality
    Then the Speciality Id, Name, and Description should be recorded correctly

  Examples:
  | Non-empty    | Non-empty    | Non-empty            | Speciality correctly added/updated             |

Scenario: Speciality Management - Confirming Speciality Editing/Updating
  Given I add/edit a Speciality
    Then the Speciality Id, Name, and Description should be displayed and modifiable

  Examples:
  | Non-empty    | Non-empty    | Non-empty            | Speciality correctly edited/updated             |

```

Note: The JSON test cases are structured to match the Gherkin scenarios. The "Examples" table in the Gherkin scenarios is represented as a list of objects with "Speciality Id", "Speciality Name", "Speciality Description", and "Expected Outcome" keys. The expected outcomes are simplified to match the input requirements, assuming that the system will behave as expected when non-empty values are provided. The actual expected outcomes would depend on the specific system's behavior and requirements, which should be detailed in the system's documentation.

This test suite addresses the functional requirements and includes scenarios for both positive and negative test cases, boundary values, and error paths. It also ensures that the test cases cover the necessary preconditions and steps to validate the system's behavior. The JSON test cases provide concrete, checkable outcomes for each scenario.
